text:
sam: Hey — noticed a handful of new hires never got the `data-analysts` role in Okta after provisioning. Deprovision worked for one person yesterday but group mapping didn't apply. Anyone seen this recently? :thinking:

jess: Hmm, saw similar on friday around 03:12 UTC. SCIM sync completed but group->app assignment step errored for some orgs. Do you have an example user id?

sam: user: u6729. Quick check: they show up in Okta as 'active' but missing group. No error in the UI.

infra-bot: SCIM sync job 2026-02-08T03:12:04Z finished. Summary: total=1, created=0, updated=1, errors=1. Error codes: 409 (conflict) for group assignment.

carlos: 409 for group assignment usually means duplicate member or mismatch in externalId mapping. Are we still using `meta.externalId` from HR feed?

diane: quick privacy/security reminder: if you paste logs, redact any access tokens or email addresses. We should avoid exposing PII in the channel. :lock:

sam: will scrub — here's a sanitized snippet (no tokens):
```
[scim-sync] user=u6729 action=assign_group group_id=ga-analytics status=409 reason="member already exists"
[scim-sync] user=u6729 action=verify_groups status=ok
```

jess: that suggests SCIM thought the member existed but the mapping layer didn't attach the app role. Could be a race between provisioning and group mapping webhook. We had a transient delay last week when HR feed batching changed.

carlos: can you check the group externalId in the HR feed and in Okta? If they differ (e.g., extra prefix), our group-mapper rejects it. Also check case-sensitivity — we recently had a lowercasing change in the mapper.

sam: confirmed HR feed externalId=GA-ANALYTICS, Okta group.externalId=ga-analytics. That mismatch matches the mapper change.

jess: ok makes sense. Short-term mitigation: we can add a compatibility mapping in the SCIM mapper to accept case-insensitive matches. I'll open a small infra PR and a canary rollout.

sam: sounds good. Do we need security approval for the mapper change? It's just acceptance logic, no credentials.

sec-team: @sam quick q — will this change alter audit logs or create ambiguous mappings? We need to ensure traceability for provisioning events.

jess: it will add a normalization step (lowercase both sides) before comparison. Audit logs will still log pre- and post-normalization externalIds. No tokens or secrets touched.

alex: tagging product: this could affect license counting if a different group id now matches. Are we okay to proceed with a short canary on 20% of orgs?

carlos: I'd prefer 10% first, given potential license assignment differences.

jess: sure — 10% canary + feature flag. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842 (draft).

sam: pinging for code review — @alex @diane any objections? :eyes:

diane: fine from security perspective if logs remain unchanged and we don't log raw HR PII. Also add a unit test for collisions (two different externalIds that normalize to same value).

alex: approve for canary 10%. Please include a rollback plan and monitoring: key metrics = group-assign-fail-rate, license-count-delta, scim-error-rate. Tag `alerts:scim` for quick paging if thresholds spike.

jess: noted. I'll add tests, canary flag, rollback steps, and a short dashboard.

okta-bot: Notice: Okta group sync scheduled at 2026-02-08T06:00:00Z for affected orgs.

infra-bot: Deploy tag infra/scim-mapper@staging queued. Will run canary on 10% orgs after tests pass.

sam: thanks all. I'll monitor affected users and share a short postmortem if we see more. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

sec-team: thanks — please keep a copy of the sanitized logs attached to the incident ticket (INC-2026-112) and mark any user-facing PII removed.

jess: creating INC-2026-112 now and linking the PR.

sam: done. Closing this thread for now, will update. :
